chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: The Baptist church as the source of jazz
summary: Danny says the singers in his Baptist church have the meters and passing tones that are the source of all jazz.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Because if you go in the Baptist Church I belong to, they got at least fifty chicks in there who can sing...sing meters and beats and never have recorded. And they would really explain something about them tempos, which I researched (which I didn't know; it was new to me) in the Baptist Church. That's the source of it all. All of that Jazz, everything that happened come right out of that Church. I hear them people doing that, and they don't know nothin' about Louis Armstrong, Coleman Hawkins, Dizzy Gillespie. But I hear them people do these sounds and these passing tones in the church...
The music that comes out of that Church is out them people. And it's primitive, it's natural -- fantastic.
